reason: a 20x-per-variant measurement of the frozen probes found a second, pre-existing abort that the single gate run could not surface

corrections.was: harness liveness calibration, not a publication defect
corrections.now: INCOMPLETE. The liveness assertion is one of TWO abort modes. The probe also aborts on its own payload-consistency assertion `move.captured_low == ~move.path_low`, which no run of the gate could have shown because it aborts earlier. That second abort is not attributed to any mechanism and is not a harness calibration issue.
corrections.unchanged_part: the liveness assertion itself is still timing-dependent and still should not be used as a gate

corrections.note: unchanged, but now for two independent reasons

new_observation.r3_tsan_both_compilers: 0/20 pass, 20/20 exit 66 (the C11 sanitizer blocker, deterministic)
new_observation.tension_recorded: the intended seqlock semantics suggest a torn payload should be impossible; the measurement contradicts that reading, and the contradiction is the finding

consequences: G2's publication-protocol scope is not closed and should not be treated as near closure
a reader that can accept an inconsistent move snapshot can hand a wrong move to the search: a correctness question that outranks the Lazy SMP performance verdict
no production change, SPRT or promotion is authorised by this measurement

next_diagnostic.first_step: a diagnostic probe that records the accepted w0/w1/w2/d plus an immediate re-read of sequence/key/move_w0/move_w1/move_w2 instead of asserting, to show whether the accepted words came from different writes
no_code_change_controls: run the same frozen probe pinned to one CPU (taskset -c 0)
repeat the 20x measurement on a host with more vCPUs (larger GitHub runners are unavailable on this repository's plan)
next_diagnostic.constraint: any change to the frozen probe, its assertions or its workload needs explicit owner acceptance and must not be made to manufacture a pass
